More than twenty years of South Florida building sit behind PGX Builders Group, along with over 150 remodels and additions, all of them permitted and inspected. faqs.q: Do I need design review to remodel a house in Surfside?

We prepare the drawings, attend the meetings, and build the board calendar into your schedule so it never becomes a surprise.

faqs.q: How long does permitting take with the Town of Surfside?
faqs.a: Longer than homeowners expect and shorter than the horror stories, provided the submission is right. Simple interior scopes move in weeks; anything requiring board review is tied to meeting dates, and complete plans must be in well ahead of them. Our approach is to submit complete, code-referenced packages the first time. Most permitting delays in this town are really resubmittal delays wearing a disguise.

faqs.q: Should we remodel our Surfside house or tear it down?
faqs.a: It depends on the structure, the elevation, and what you want the house to be. FEMA's substantial-improvement rules can limit how much you invest in a house sitting below current flood elevation, which sometimes tips the decision. Plenty of Surfside homes are worth keeping: good bones, real character, mature streets. We will walk it with you and give you a straight answer, even when that answer is not a remodel.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to remodel a whole house in Surfside?

What we can promise: we work at the high end of the market, we price from a fixed written scope rather than an allowance-padded guess, and the figure you sign is the figure we defend. If a hard budget conversation needs to happen, we would rather have it before demolition than after.

faqs.q: There is an open permit on my Surfside house from a previous owner. What now?
faqs.a: First we pull the record at the Town of Surfside Building Department and find out what the permit actually covered and how far it got. Sometimes the work was finished and only the final inspection was missed. Sometimes the work was never done, or was done differently, and the honest route is a revision or a new permit. Either way it takes weeks rather than days, so start it before a closing date rather than after one.

faqs.q: Who issues building permits in Surfside, the town or Miami-Dade County?
faqs.a: The Town of Surfside Building Department issues and inspects permits for property inside the town limits. County rules still reach the job: Miami-Dade product approvals for hurricane-rated components, and the county recertification code for buildings other than houses and duplexes. Exterior work and substantial renovations also route through the Planning and Zoning Board for design review, which runs on a meeting calendar. Nobody expedites that calendar. You submit early and you submit complete.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to replace windows or the roof in Surfside?
faqs.a: Yes, both, and both come with product documentation. Surfside sits inside the High-Velocity Hurricane Zone, so glazing, doors, and roof assemblies need current Miami-Dade approvals, and the installation has to match the method in that approval, including fasteners and anchorage. Inspectors check the paperwork and the wall together. Unpermitted window swaps are one of the most common findings we clean up here, usually years later, usually under a deadline someone else set.

faqs.q: Our building received a recertification notice. Can PGX do the repair work?
faqs.a: Yes. We do not sign the report, because that belongs to your engineer or architect, but we build what it calls for: concrete restoration, balcony and railing work, waterproofing, electrical corrections, and the permits and inspections that close each item out. In a town that has lived through what Surfside lived through, boards want documentation rather than reassurance. We work to your engineer of record and to the association's schedule and access rules.

faqs.q: What does it cost to fix a permit problem?
faqs.a: It depends on what the record shows and how much of the work has to be opened up to prove it. A missed final inspection is a modest exercise. A wall built without a permit, or a bathroom that needs a plumbing test, is a project. Town fees belong to the town and we pass them through at cost. Our part is priced from a written scope after we have read the file, never guessed at over the phone.

permitting-compliance.cta_heading: Let us pull the permit history
permitting-compliance.cta_sub: Send the address. We will check what is open, tell you what closing it takes, and put the number in writing, in English o en español.
